tool.name: Plot 3D peakmaps
tool.description: from a collection of mzML files
tool.command: mkdir -p 'mzml' && #for $f in $input_files: ln -s '${f}' 'mzml/${f.element_identifier}.${f.ext}' && #end for python3 '${__tool_directory__}/main.py' --mzml_folder 'mzml' --rt-min $rt_min --rt-max $rt_max --mz-min $mz_min --mz-max $mz_max #if str($colouring.mode) == 'ion': --no-colour-all --ion-mz $colouring.ion_mz --ion-rt $colouring.ion_rt --mz-to-colour-ppm $colouring.mz_to_colour_ppm --rt-to-colour $colouring.rt_to_colour #end if --annotation '${annotation}' #if $title: --title '${title}' #end if --colorscale '${advanced.colorscale}' --panel-width $advanced.panel_width --panel-height $advanced.panel_height --panels-per-row $advanced.panels_per_row --max-live-plots $advanced.max_live_plots --output '$report'

param.name: input_files
param.label: Input mzML files
param.help: Every file of the collection becomes one panel titled after its element identifier; files without peaks inside the displayed window are skipped. Avoid the glob special characters '[', '*' and '?' in the identifiers.

param.name: rt_min
param.label: Lowest retention time to display
param.help: In the time unit of the mzML files.

param.name: rt_max
param.label: Highest retention time to display
param.help: In the time unit of the mzML files; has to be larger than the lowest retention time.

param.name: mz_max
param.label: Highest m/z to display
param.help: Has to be larger than the lowest m/z.

param.name: mode
param.label: Colouring mode
param.help: Colour every peak of the displayed window, or only the peaks around one selected ion and draw everything else lightgray.
param.option: Colour every peak of the displayed window
Colour only the box around one ion

param.name: ion_mz
param.label: m/z of the ion to colour
param.help: Centre of the coloured m/z box.

param.name: ion_rt
param.label: Retention time of the ion to colour
param.help: Centre of the coloured retention time box, in the time unit of the mzML files.

param.name: mz_to_colour_ppm
param.label: Half width of the coloured m/z box (ppm)
param.help: In ppm of the ion m/z.

param.name: rt_to_colour
param.label: Half width of the coloured retention time box
param.help: In the time unit of the mzML files.

param.name: annotation
param.label: Annotation
param.help: Name of the coloured region; it is the legend entry and part of the default report title.

param.name: title
param.label: Report title
param.help: Leave empty to use the default ('<annotation> in raw data').

param.name: colorscale
param.label: Colour scale
param.help: Plotly colourscale of the coloured peaks.

param.name: panel_height
param.label: Panel height
param.help: Height of every panel in pixels.

param.name: panels_per_row
param.label: Panels per row
param.help: Largest number of panels next to each other.

param.name: max_live_plots
param.label: Maximum live plots
param.help: Hard limit of plotly graphs the browser may keep alive at once (WebGL context budget). Do not raise above about 10 unless the report freezes in your browser.

tool.help:
.. class:: infomark
**What it does**
Reads every mzML file of the input collection, cuts it to the retention time and m/z window you ask for and writes **one HTML file with one 3D peakmap panel per measurement**. All panels share
- the same rotation (drag one plot, every plot follows), - the same rt / m/z / intensity window, - the same ``log10(intensity + 1)`` colour scale, which is drawn once in the header.
**Input**
- A list collection of mzML files. Every file becomes one panel titled after its element identifier; files without peaks inside the displayed window are skipped. - The displayed retention time and m/z window (the minimum has to be smaller than the maximum in both dimensions).
**Colouring mode**
- *Colour every peak of the displayed window*: every peak inside the displayed window is coloured with the shared colour scale. - *Colour only the box around one ion*: only the peaks inside the m/z and retention time box around the selected ion are coloured (both bounds inclusive), everything else is drawn flat lightgray.
**Peak aggregation**
Panels with more than 2500 peaks in the displayed window are aggregated so the report stays responsive: the rt / m/z plane is divided into a 50 x 50 grid and every cell is drawn as one stem at the cell centre whose height is the mean intensity of the peaks of that cell (coloured and grey peaks are averaged separately). Individual peaks may therefore not be visible, and bar heights are cell averages rather than exact peak intensities. The intensity axis and the colour scale are scaled to the bars that are actually drawn, so they can differ between the colouring modes and from the raw peak intensities.
**Output**
A single self-contained HTML report - plotly is bundled into the file, so it can be opened offline. Panels are created while you scroll and thrown away again when they leave the page, never more than *Maximum live plots* of them at a time, so a collection with a hundred measurements does not run out of WebGL contexts. The header has a filter for the file names, checkboxes for sync rotation and sync axes, a *Reset all views* button and the shared colour bar. The panel that you are dragging is outlined in blue; the caption of every panel shows how many peaks it holds and how many of them are annotated.
